loaded_skill.content:
---
name: data-agent-query
version: 6
---
Load this skill when planning or querying. Its content and hash stay frozen for the run.

Plan explicit requirements. Use kind=read_node with source_id and node_id whenever complete chapter reading is required. The host tracks required, returned and unread body IDs, rejects premature finish and preserves remaining gaps.

Use kind=query with an explicit QueryPlan for numeric requirements. Records, entity, periods and formula must match that requirement and its pinned execution scope. The host verifies returned records, source citations, registered calculation and exact operands; Business text alone cannot satisfy a margin requirement. QueryPlan does not select currency: record units remain explicit in results and the registered calculation rejects incompatible operand units or accounting bases. Fiscal-year mappings must belong to the requested entity's company; another company's mapping cannot fill a missing mapping.

Use kind=source_evidence with an explicit scoped source_id and no node_id when the task only asks to deliver or verify original text/table. The host requires complete body blocks from that source actually delivered to this role; a record, citation, navigation hit or Worker handoff cannot satisfy it. This does not require reading a full chapter and does not establish semantic correctness by itself.

Use kind=source_answer when the task asks a narrative question, such as the categories or reasons disclosed in a source. Reading a related paragraph is insufficient. Submit action=answer for exactly one requirement, with claims containing statement, temporal_basis, period_context and citations using the Extraction fields (context_id, block_id, quote, label). Every quote must come from a fully delivered block in that requirement's pinned source and scope. Separate reported_actual, forward_looking, not_period_specific and unclear. Read the introduction and full list when the task requires categories; do not infer completeness from one relevant passage.

An answer must declare model_claimed_coverage, coverage_note and unresolved_questions. partial requires concrete unresolved questions; claimed_complete requires none but remains a model judgment. The host validates references, never semantic completeness. No answer prevents finish unless an explicit gap is recorded; a partial answer seals a partial result. research_answers persists bounded candidate answers and artifact pointers across later reading. Revising an answer preserves old versions; changing only statement or label is not new evidence. Worker answers are untrusted candidates and do not satisfy the parent's requirements.

General information requirements only check metadata references and remain semantically unreviewed; do not use them to represent original-body verification. Plan revisions append requirements, preserving earlier requirements and gaps. If a new source or snapshot is required, retain the original requirement and explain its gap, then append a requirement bound to the new scope.

Outline and search return navigation only. New node/hit locations and validated source/snapshot transitions count as exploration progress, never as body reading. Read indicated body blocks before citing; use retained IDs to reread evidence. Reaching a chapter end does not establish earlier coverage. Repeated results, repeated errors and reworded reasons do not reset the three-turn no-progress limit.

source_leads persists already-located blocks with exact read_context parameters and role-local reading status. Use those entries instead of repeatedly reopening the outline. pending_body_reads identifies requested target text omitted from previews; follow its exact artifact pointer until delivered. retained_body re-presents bounded complete blocks already read by this role, including nearby units, so they remain available together. Omitted blocks are explicitly counted, not summarized. An index_id is not a node_id; use actual outline node IDs.

The initial catalog contains first pages only. Use discover_catalog(kind, cursor) and probe_schema(filters, cursor) to inspect additional sources, entities, metrics, fiscal mappings and scoped examples. Preserve filters when continuing a catalog cursor. A missing first-page item does not establish missing data. Full legacy query/task schemas are not repeated in each input.

When preparation metadata is supplied, inspect its filing catalog and callback contracts through the registered preparation artifact. The newest annual filing may not cover the requested year's Business chapter. Acquire the explicitly discovered reporting period, then materialize the returned source_run_id, before using its data; confirm the fiscal-year label from that source rather than extrapolating a calendar. Missing or incomplete filing discovery remains an explicit gap.

Tool receipts distinguish execution limits from preview truncation and link to the complete saved output. Use read_artifact(artifact_id, pointer, cursor) for bounded JSON array items, object entries or text character ranges; list_artifacts discovers other saved outputs. Respect the original artifact scope/hash. Read the evidence index's next page when needed; indexes themselves are immutable paginated artifacts. An oversized item exposes a child pointer or the budget needed to read it. Saving text to disk does not count as reading it: only complete blocks, or all character ranges of a block, actually delivered in planner inputs advance body coverage. Extraction is restricted to delivered source blocks. The final v2 evidence bundle references immutable artifacts; consumers may load original content separately.

For broad questions, record uncovered requirements as gaps instead of declaring completion. Finish means the explicit host checks passed, not that research semantics were approved. Never invent numeric arithmetic or automatically adopt evidence.

claims.statement: Alphabet discloses that its capital investments in property and equipment consist primarily of two major categories: (1) technical infrastructure, which consists of investments in servers and network equipment, data center land, and building construction and improvements; and (2) office facilities, ground-up development projects, and building improvements.
claims.period_context: Alphabet FY2025 10-K, Capital Expenditures and Leases / Capital Expenditures disclosure, page 38; the category disclosure is not tied to a single fiscal year in the read block.

citations.label: Capital expenditures categories introduction

claims.period_context: Forward-looking statement for 2026 relative to 2025, Alphabet FY2025 10-K, page 38.

citations.label: Forward-looking capital expenditure expectation

value.coverage_note: Read the Capital Expenditures and Leases / Capital Expenditures section on page 38, including the introduction and the complete two-item category list, plus the following paragraph containing reported 2024/2025 capital expenditure amounts and the 2026 forward-looking statement. This covers the requested capital-expenditure major-use disclosure categories without inferring maintenance capex or AI investment returns.

items.text: Our capital investments in property and equipment consist primarily of the following major categories:
•technical infrastructure, which consists of our investments in servers and network equipment, data center land, and building construction and improvements; and
•office facilities, ground-up development projects, and building improvements.

Assets not yet in service are those that are not ready for their intended use, including assets in the process of construction or assembly, and consist primarily of technical infrastructure. The time frame from date of purchase to placement in service of these assets may extend from months to years. For example, our data center construction projects are generally multi-year projects with multiple phases, where we acquire land and buildings, construct buildings, and secure and install servers and network equipment.

During the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2025, we spent $52.5 billion and $91.4 billion on capital expenditures, respectively. In 2026, we expect to significantly increase, relative to 2025, our investment in our technical infrastructure, including servers and network equipment, and data centers. Depreciation of our property and equipment commences when such assets are ready for their intended use. For the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2025, our depreciation on property and equipment was $15.3 billion and $21.1 billion, respectively.

As of December 31, 2025, the amount of total undiscounted future lease payments under operating leases was $18.3 billion, of which $3.3 billion is short-term, and total undiscounted future lease payments under finance leases was $2.9 billion, of which $491 million is short-term.

As of December 31, 2025, we have entered into leases primarily related to data centers that have not yet commenced with short-term and long-term future lease payments of $5.8 billion and $52.7 billion, respectively. These leases will commence between 2026 and 2031 with non-cancelable lease terms primarily between one and 25 years.

Changes to US tax law enacted on July 4, 2025, allow for immediate expensing of domestic research and experimentation costs, accelerated depreciation on eligible capital expenditures, and other tax law changes impacting 2025 with certain changes effective in 2026. These changes are reflected in our results for the year ended December 31, 2025.

•In 2025, we entered into definitive agreements to acquire Wiz, a leading cloud security platform, for $32.0 billion, and Intersect, a provider of data center and energy infrastructure solutions, for $4.8 billion in cash plus the assumption of debt. Both acquisitions are expected to close in 2026, subject to customary closing conditions, including the receipt of regulatory approvals.
•In 2025, we issued senior unsecured notes for net proceeds of $37.3 billion, to be used for general corporate purposes.
•OI&E of $29.8 billion for the year ended December 31, 2025 included net gains on equity securities of $24.1 billion, primarily related to unrealized gains on our non-marketable equity securities.

•Other Bets operating loss of $7.5 billion for the year ended December 31, 2025 included a $2.1 billion employee compensation charge recognized in the fourth quarter for Waymo, primarily reflected in research and development expenses, based on estimated stock valuation. In February 2026, Waymo announced an investment round of $16.0 billion, the significant majority of which was funded by Alphabet.
